    AI Overview
    The Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team last won the NCAA National Championship in
    1989. Led by interim head coach Steve Fisher and tournament standout Glen Rice, the Wolverines defeated Seton Hall 80-79 in overtime. This remains the program's only NCAA men's basketball national title. 
    • Year: 1989
    • Result: Michigan 80, Seton Hall 79 (OT)
    • Key Performers: Glen Rice (Tournament MOP), Rumeal Robinson
    • Significance: Michigan became the first team to win 30 games in a season and won their first championship.
    • Subsequent Appearances: Michigan has reached the championship game since (1992, 1993, 2013, 2018) but lost all four. 
    Note: The results indicate a 2026 National Championship matchup against UConn is occurring.

    AI Overview
    Yes, the
    University of Michigan men's basketball team has won one NCAA national championship    , defeating Seton Hall 80–79 in overtime to win the 1989 tournament under interim head coach Steve Fisher. The Wolverines have appeared in the Final Four nine times (1964, 1965, 1976, 1989, 1992*, 1993*, 2013, 2018, 2026). 
    • 1989 Championship: Led by Glen Rice (who set a tournament record for points) and Rumeal Robinson, Michigan went 6-0 under Fisher.
    • Final Four History: Michigan reached the title game in 1965, 1976, 1992, 1993, 2013, and 2018, finishing as runner-up in those years.
    • Finals Appearances: Note: The 1992 and 1993 appearances were later vacated due to NCAA infractions related to the Fab Five scandal, though they reached the championship game
      .
    • Latest Appearance: The team advanced to the 2026 Final Four.
